title: Code smells and refactorings
idea: A code smell is a surface symptom, like a long method or a copied rule, that hints at a design problem; each smell has a known refactoring.
points: A smell is a hint, not a bug: confirm it hurts before you refactor.
Fix one smell at a time, keep behaviour unchanged, rerun checks each step.
Duplicated rules cause shotgun surgery; move the rule into the class owning its data.
Flag arguments and magic numbers are covered in c05-t04; this page shows structural smells.

hero.title: Five smells you will meet in review
head: Smell
Symptom in a review
Refactoring
rows: You scroll to see one method; comments mark its sections
Extract method, one name per step
The same rule pasted into two classes
Keep the rule once; both callers use it
One business change edits several files, and one gets missed
Move the rule into the class that owns its data
Months, ages and money passed around as bare int and long
renew(x, true, false) and a bare 4000 in many places
hero.caption: Name the smell, then apply its refactoring in small, behaviour-preserving steps.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: A long method and a discount rule copied into two classes. Every call compiles and returns a believable total.

walk.text: Long method: four commented sections, each a step that deserves its own name.
The student discount was raised to 20% here, in one of its two homes.
Duplicated code: `Receipts` repeats the rule and still says 15%. Shotgun surgery missed one file.
Primitive obsession: age and months are bare `int` values, so a negative term is accepted.
Run it: the receipt disagrees with the charge, and a negative renewal prints a refund.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: Each section has a named home and the discount lives in one place. Rejecting a negative term changes behaviour, so it ships in its own commit.

walk.text: Replace primitive with a record: `Term` checks its range once, so no invalid term exists.
`Money` owns arithmetic and formatting; callers stop rebuilding the decimal string.
Move method: the discount reads age, so it lives on `Member`. One edit changes it everywhere.
Extract method: the long method's steps are now named calls that read like the rule.
`Receipt` is handed the price instead of recomputing it. The duplicate is gone.
Charge and receipt now agree, and a negative term fails at the edge.

pitfalls: Refactoring and changing behaviour in one commit makes a broken total impossible to trace.
Renaming a smell away: `renewV2` with the same bare ints is still primitive obsession.
Chasing every smell in old code; fix the ones in the file you must change.

quiz.q: In the smelly version, what does this call print?
quiz.why: `Receipts` holds its own copy of the discount, still at 15%: 12000 minus 1800 is 10200 cents. Only the copy in `Renewals` was updated.

takeaway: Name the smell, pick its refactoring, change one thing at a time.
